title: SWE-Shift: Evaluating Coding Agents in Evolving Workspaces
abstract: arXiv:2610.32196v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Repository-level coding benchmarks largely assume that tasks and environments remain unchanged throughout execution. In software development, code, dependencies, runtime state, and requirements can change while an agent is still working. We introduce SWE-Shift, a benchmark for evaluating coding agents under such mid-execution changes. From the same saved history and workspace, a Clean continuation proceeds without intervention, while a matched Shifted continuation receives a task-relevant update. Success requires completing the current task, preserving still-valid work, and satisfying the applicable state and evidence checks. The benchmark contains 120 scenarios across 12 change families, each evaluated at nine scheduled intervention positions. translated_title: SWE-Shift：在动态演变的工作区中评估编程智能体
translated_abstract: 仓库级编程基准测试在很大程度上假设任务和环境在整个执行过程中保持不变。而在软件开发中，代码、依赖项、运行时状态和需求可能在智能体仍在工作时发生变化。我们提出了 SWE-Shift，一个用于评估编程智能体在执行中途遭遇变化时表现的基准。基于相同的保存历史和工作区，Clean（干净）延续在不干预的情况下继续进行，而与之匹配的 Shifted（转变）延续则会收到与任务相关的更新。成功需要完成当前任务、保留仍然有效的工作，并满足适用的状态和证据检查。该基准包含横跨 12 个变化族别的 120 个场景，每个场景在九个预定的干预位置进行评估。我们评估了 17 个编程智能体系统，所有系统在 Shifted 条件下的成功率均低于 Clean 条件。GPT-6 Astra 的成功率从 67.35% 降至 24.79%，配对成功率为 20.34%，工具/会话变化和过时证据是主要失败因素之一。
tldr: 提出 SWE-Shift 基准，用于评估编程智能体在任务执行中途遭遇代码、依赖和需求等变化时的表现，实验发现所有 17 个被测智能体系统在发生此类变化时成功率均显著下降。
en_tdlr: Introduces SWE-Shift, a benchmark evaluating coding agents under mid-execution changes to code, dependencies, and requirements, showing that all 17 evaluated agent systems suffer significant success rate drops when such changes occur.
